candidates.designation: BD+00 444 c, 'sub-Neptune-mass planet candidate' (Naponiello et al. 2025, abstract, Sect. 5.1, Table 2)
candidates.tier_reason: Single-instrument (HARPS-N, 97 RVs over ~1.5 yr) RV signal. The two-planet model beats the one-planet model by only Delta lnZ = 3.2 in the circular case, below the authors' own threshold of 5, and they say the candidate 'necessitates further observations and stronger statistical evidence to be confirmed'. The 97 d peak is absent from the activity indices, but the star shows ~45 d (S index, Na I) and ~179 d (Halpha, CCF area) periodicities, roughly half and double the candidate period. No follow-up since.
candidates.orbit_flags: RV only (HARPS-N). K = 1.73 -0.37/+0.34 m/s, T0 = 2459235.2 -6.2/+6.4 BJD, a/R* = 120 +/- 3, Teq 283 +/- 4 K (zero albedo), omega unconstrained, e < 0.50 at 1 sigma. Non-transiting as far as TESS coverage goes (predicted transit outside TESS data; posterior transit probability ~1%). Inclination unknown; paper argues true mass within a factor 2 of Msini. Paper calls it habitable-zone.
candidates.reference: Naponiello, L. et al. 2025, A&A 693, A7, 'The GAPS programme at TNG LXIV: An inner eccentric sub-Neptune and an outer sub-Neptune-mass candidate around BD+00 444 (TOI-2443)', Table 2, Sect. 4.2, 5.1

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope: GJ 160.2 b (confirmed tab, P 5.2354 d, Tuomi+2014) should be reviewed for a move off the confirmed tab: Feng et al. 2020, ApJS 246, 11 (arXiv 2001.02577) 'fail to confirm GJ 27.1 b, GJ 160.2 b, GJ 682 b and c reported by T14'; 'the 5.2-day signal ... is unlikely to be Keplerian and might arise from data reduction'. Tuomi et al. 2019 (Appendix A.7) also could not recover it and got 9.75 d instead (filed here as an 'unlikely' candidate). NASA and OEC still list b; exoplanet.eu has silently replaced its period with 9.7471 d.

HIP 55507 b (confirmed tab, Feng+2022, 2586 M_E / 8.14 MJ, P 5138 d) appears to be the known stellar companion HIP 55507 B: Xuan et al. 2024 (ApJ, arXiv 2312.02297, Sect. 8.1) give B a dynamical mass of 88.0 MJup at a ~38 au, e 0.40, say its luminosity is 'consistent with a low-mass star and not a 5.0 MJup planet', and cannot reproduce Feng's solution with Feng's data. Recommend moving it to Rejected candidates and adding HIP 55507 B (M7.5) as a stellar companion (Systems row says 1 star; SIMBAD spectral type 'K6V+M7.5', WDS J11221+4655AB).

HIP 86221 distance vs the 100 ly cut: Gaia DR3 gives the unresolved A+B pair (source 4595441941016988672) only a 2-parameter solution, no parallax. The sheet's 96.18 ly is the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) 33.91 +/- 3.88 mas. The system's only Gaia parallax is on component C (Gaia DR3 4595441868000475520 = NLTT 45161, 9.4 arcsec from A; the sheet's own multistars row calls it bound): 31.0655 +/- 0.0151 mas = 104.99 ly (Gaia DR2: 31.090 mas). If C is bound, the system lies outside 100 ly (parallax < 32.616 mas). Writer's judgement.

Small Systems-tab distance mismatches vs Gaia DR3 (3261.56/plx): HIP 70849 78.46 vs 78.66 ly (plx 41.4618); HIP 55507 83.13 vs 82.95 (39.3187); HIP 12961 76.23 vs 76.40 (42.6929); GJ 900 A 67.86 vs 68.00 (47.9641); TOI-2018 91.31 vs 91.45 (35.6664). GJ 338 A Systems row: its gaia_dr3_source_id 1022456104850892928 is GJ 338 B (HD 79211, the planet host) per SIMBAD and NASA; GJ 338 A (HD 79210) is Gaia DR3 1022456139210632064 (plx 157.8879 mas per SIMBAD). Harmless if the column is meant to carry the planet host's id.

eps Ind A b orbit on the confirmed tab (P 19205.51 d, a 12.82 au, 2066 M_E) is the pre-JWST RV/astrometry solution. The JWST-era solutions differ: NASA default (Sanghi et al. 2026) P = 25450 d; Matthews et al. 2026 (ps table) P = 39400 d; arXiv 2603.08780 gives mass 7.6 +/- 0.7 MJ and e 0.24 +0.11/-0.08; exoplanet.eu gives a = 28.4 au. Recommend updating.
TOI-2427 b mass cell is empty on the Systems tab ('TOI-2427 b:?'): Schmerling et al. 2025 (A&A 699, A185) measure Mp = 5.69 +/- ~0.55 M_E, Rp = 1.64 R_E.
HD 147379 is a gravitationally bound binary with GJ 617 B (M dwarf, V = 10.6), per Stalport et al. 2023 (arXiv 2308.05669, Sect. 2.2.2); the Systems row says 1 star.
HIP 70849 has a T4.5 brown-dwarf companion at ~9000 au (Lodieu et al. 2014); the Systems row says 1 star (may be intentional if brown dwarfs are not counted as stars).
HIP 34222 is 'GJ 265 A' / WDS J07057+2728A in SIMBAD, implying a catalogued visual companion; the Systems row says 1 star. Not investigated further (outside scope).

Paredes et al. 2021 (AJ 162, 176; arXiv 2111.15028) describe both HIP 34222 b and HIP 86221 b as 'new candidate exoplanets' (HIP 86221 b from 9 CHIRON RVs, in a 0.29 arcsec A-B binary whose host component is only presumed to be A). NASA/OEC/exoplanet.eu list both as confirmed; no independent confirmation found.
